{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed and drew the sketch the table built from: one line over the back to a flared tail and one round the belly, both leaving from the nose. That gave us a single connected run that could fall from one push. I laid the whole back line from the start domino to the nose, and then the belly's lower stretch out to the tail tip. Our check showed all 125 of 125 dominoes connected to the start, so the full fish should fall.

Execution: I checked the nose join once the back line arrived and confirmed the belly would get the fall. I split the long belly into two strokes so it could be built in parallel, and I added the second stroke to the sketch for that. I laid my stretch to pick up where Sofia stopped, and I inspected the middle after it was done. I then kept my hands off the table so nobody bumped anything before the push.

Collaboration: I kept the table's roles clear: Sofia on the belly, Omar and Jack watching for gaps and the tail end. When two people were about to lay the same stroke, I said so quickly so we didn't collide. I also explained that the push starts at the tail end, so the belly only gets the fall once the back line reaches the nose, and that helped Sofia time her start.

Leadership: I helped set direction early by getting a sketch on the pad that everyone could build from. I called the plan for splitting the belly and said where each person's section started and ended. In the last minutes I kept the table calm and hands-off until the push.

I believe my share of the table's result was about 40 percent, since I did the sketch, the back line and the lower belly, and the other three built the upper belly, checked joins and kept the table steady.", "my_share_percent": 40}
